title: Delhi Court Sentences Tahir Hussain to Life in Prison for IB Officer's Murder During 2020 Riots
excerpt: A Delhi sessions court rejected the prosecution's demand for the death penalty and sentenced the former AAP councillor and four co-accused to life imprisonment for the killing of Intelligence Bureau staffer Ankit Sharma during the 2020 northeast Delhi communal violence.
body:
• Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh of Karkardooma Court sentenced Tahir Hussain and four others — Nazir, Asim, Javed and Anas — to life imprisonment for the murder of IB officer Ankit Sharma during the February 2020 Delhi riots.
  • The court rejected Delhi Police's demand for the death penalty, which prosecutors had argued was warranted given the "cold-blooded" nature of the killing that left 51 wounds on Sharma's body.
  • Hussain, a former Aam Aadmi Party councillor, was convicted on July 13 under multiple IPC sections including murder, kidnapping, rioting and promoting enmity, but acquitted of criminal conspiracy charges.
  • The case is among the most high-profile from the 2020 northeast Delhi riots, which claimed 53 lives and became a flashpoint in India's political and communal landscape.

A Delhi sessions court on Thursday sentenced former Aam Aadmi Party councillor Tahir Hussain and four co-accused to life imprisonment for the murder of Intelligence Bureau officer Ankit Sharma during the 2020 northeast Delhi communal riots. Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh of the Karkardooma Court rejected the prosecution's push for the death penalty, opting instead for the maximum custodial term short of capital punishment.

The sentencing concludes a six-year legal battle over one of the most brutal killings from the February 2020 violence, which engulfed parts of northeast Delhi and left 53 people dead.

The Crime and Conviction

Ankit Sharma, a 26-year-old IB staffer, left his home in the Khajuri Khas area on the evening of February 25, 2020, to buy groceries. He never returned. His body, bearing 51 injuries — 18 inflicted with sharp-edged weapons — was recovered the following day from a drain near Chand Bagh Pulia.

The FIR was lodged at Dayalpur police station by Sharma's father, Ravinder Kumar, who alleged that Hussain, then a municipal councillor whose office was nearby, had gathered associates and incited violence in the area. On July 13, after examining 91 prosecution witnesses and a substantial body of documentary, medical, forensic and electronic evidence, the court convicted Hussain and four others — Nazir, Asim, Javed and Anas — under multiple sections of the Indian Penal Code, including Section 302 (murder), 365 (kidnapping), 153A (promoting enmity between groups), 147 and 148 (rioting), and 149 (unlawful assembly).

Six other co-accused, including Hussain's brother Shoaib Alam, were acquitted of all charges. Hussain himself was acquitted of criminal conspiracy under Section 120B.

Death Penalty Rejected

The sentencing phase saw sharp arguments from both sides. Special Public Prosecutor Madhukar Pandey urged the court to impose the death penalty, describing the killing as a case where "people turned into butchers."

"Ankit Sharma was abducted and relentlessly assaulted before he was killed. A total of 51 wounds were found on his body, 18 of these were inflicted with sharp weapons. They fell to the level of being animals. Even after the victim died, they kept on the assault."

— Madhukar Pandey, Special Public Prosecutor

Pandey argued that the murder should not be viewed in isolation but in the context of the broader riots that killed 53 people. "Those who want mercy should also show mercy," he told the court, according to Bar and Bench.

Defence counsel countered that the death penalty can only be imposed in the "rarest of rare" cases. They argued that the judgment established the presence of a mob at the crime scene but did not detail the specific role of each convict in the killing. The defence also pointed to Hussain's good conduct in prison during his more than six years in custody.

Judge Singh ultimately opted for life imprisonment, declining to classify the case as meeting the rarest-of-rare threshold required for capital punishment under Indian law.

The Political Fallout

The case has carried significant political weight since it first emerged during the riots. Hussain was suspended by the Aam Aadmi Party after his involvement came to light, and the case became a recurring point of attack against the party by political opponents. In the 2020 Delhi Assembly elections, Hussain had contested from the Mustafabad constituency on an AIMIM ticket after being dropped by AAP, finishing third with 33,474 votes.

The court's finding that Hussain was part of an unlawful assembly that had gathered "with animus against Hindus" at Chand Bagh Pulia added a communal dimension to the verdict. The judgment stated that the assembly shared "a common object to commit rioting, loot, arson and to cause damage to the property and person of the members of the Hindu community," according to LiveLaw.

Diaspora Significance

The 2020 Delhi riots drew global attention and condemnation, with diaspora organisations and international media closely following the legal proceedings. The Ankit Sharma case, involving the killing of a government intelligence officer during communal violence, became emblematic of the broader crisis. The sentencing is likely to be watched closely by Indian diaspora communities as a measure of judicial accountability for riot-related violence.

What Comes Next

The convicted men retain the right to appeal the sentence before the Delhi High Court. Given the severity of the charges and the political profile of the case, an appeal is widely expected. The Enforcement Directorate has also filed a separate chargesheet against Hussain alleging money laundering of Rs 1.10 crore to instigate anti-CAA protests and the Delhi riots — a case that remains pending.

The verdict marks a significant milestone in the adjudication of the 2020 Delhi riots cases, many of which have moved slowly through India's overburdened courts. With over 750 FIRs registered in connection with the violence, the Ankit Sharma murder case stands as one of the few to reach a definitive conclusion at the trial court level.
